l1_freya: Okay, can we talk about A.I. for a second? Everybody is using it, but many people still do not understand the risk that matters most. When generative A.I. does not have reliable information, it can produce an answer that sounds completely confident, but is simply wrong. There is a name for that. Hallucination. And it is not just a harmless glitch. Lawyers have submitted court filings containing cases and quotations that did not exist, because they relied on A.I. without verifying the work. By the end of twenty twenty-five, researchers had documented hundreds of court matters worldwide involving suspected or confirmed A.I. generated errors. So when you use A.I. for something consequential, your job, your money, or your rights, remember one rule. A.I. can be an extraordinary assistant, but it should never be your final authority. Let it help organize. Do not let it make the legal decision. And have a human verify what matters. That principle is built into one3seven. You provide the actual records. one3seven organizes the documented events and connects surfaced information back to its source, so the worker and the reviewing firm can inspect the original record themselves. It does not declare that the law was violated. It does not predict the outcome. It does not ask anyone to trust an unsupported A.I. conclusion. It organizes and reflects. The human reviews and decides. So yes, use A.I. Just use A.I. that shows you its receipts.
